newsitem.title: USA: Ford may buy Lions stadium name rights - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ford may buy Lions stadium name rights - paper.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's board of directors is expected to announce Thursday whether to buy rights to name a proposed new downtown football stadium for the Detroit Lions, The Detroit News reported on Tuesday.
The automaker would pay $30 million to $40 million for the rights to name the domed facility, providing a major financing boost for the $225 million project, the newspaper said.
"There is nothing to announce at this time," a Ford spokesman Ed Miller said on Tuesday. Ford has not chosen a specific name for the facility, the newspaper said.
Ford's board of directors, which includes Lions owners William Clay Ford and his son, William Clay Ford Jr., has a regular meeting scheduled on Thursday.

The Lions face a Nov. 1 deadline to attract $50 million in corporate and private contributions to help finance the project, a sum that would include any proceeds from sale of name rights to the stadium.
Plans for the 65,000 seat football dome, which would be built next to an open-air baseball stadium for the Detroit Tigers in downtown Detroit were announced in August.
The Lions would leave the 80,000-seat Pontiac Silverdome in suburban Pontiac, Mich., where they have played for the past 21 years. The team's Silverdome lease expires in 2004.

The Detroit News, quoting unnamed sources, said William Clay Ford and William Clay Ford Jr., two of three Ford family members on the Ford Motor Co board of directors, may abstain from any board votes on acquiring the stadium name rights.
The other Ford family member on the automaker's board, Edsel Ford II, does not own an interest in the Lions.
The Detroit Free Press also reported Tuesday that Chrysler Corp. was interested acquiring rights to the stadium name.
"We have been approached regarding the proposal, but we can't discuss it further," said Chrysler spokeswoman Rita McKay.

Mayor Dennis Archer has approached Ford, Chrysler and General Motors Corp. for contributions to the project within the past few weeks. Archer's initial plans reportedly called for equal funding by the three automakers, with the proposed name, "Motordome."
